note: Element definitions live in data, not code. Adding an element means editing this file (spec 3.2). Ids are declared here and are permanent: they are baked into saves and world hashes, so reordering this list must never change behaviour. Id 0 is reserved for empty space.
valueNote: `value` is what a cell is worth to a press, in points. A press takes only what has value, so zero also means the machine ignores it entirely and lets it fall through. `currency` marks the element those points are pressed into: currency has no value of its own, so no press ever takes it back, and currency inside a vault is the player's balance. `refinedInto` is separate from all of that: it names what a Refine machine (a burner, a compactor) turns this element into, one cell at a time, regardless of value.
heatNote: `melting_point`/`boiling_point` are Kelvin; `thermal_conductivity` decides how fast a cell trades heat with whatever touches it (spec 5.3) — a heater is the source, everything else just conducts. `meltsInto`/`boilsInto` name what this becomes once its own temperature reaches the matching point; absent means nothing does, which is still true of most of the roster. Checked hottest-first, so something hot enough to boil never gets stuck being evaluated as merely melted.

elements.note: Currency, and matter like everything else. A press turns product into nuggets; a nugget only counts as money once a vault is holding it (spec 5.1). Denser than anything else here, because it is gold — it sinks through water to the bottom of a vault.
elements.name: gold

elements.note: The byproduct of pressing. Denser than sand and wet sand, so it settles below them in a mixed pile rather than mixing back in; far short of gold, so it never buries a nugget. Burns into burntResidue (spec 5.3) — a burner is the intended consumer, not the press itself.
elements.name: residue

elements.note: The next stage: what a burner leaves behind. Denser again — burning drives off what was loose in it — and, once compacted, waiting to be fuel.
elements.name: burntResidue

elements.note: The end of the chain so far: nothing burns it yet, and nothing spends it. A generic heater is the intended consumer (spec 5.3), not one machine built just for this.
elements.name: fuel

elements.note: Not matter the player ever sees fall or pile up — it is what `World::place` fills a belt's own footprint with (spec 4.1), so gravity holds cargo up on it the same way it holds anything up on solid ground. Solid, so it already never moves; the density is absurd anyway, purely as a second guarantee against ever being displaced. `internal` is client-only (sim-core never reads it) and hides this row from any player-facing element picker, since it is scenery, not a material anyone chooses.
elements.name: beltStructure

elements.note: What sand becomes past its melting point (spec 5.3) — a real liquid immediately, not a dead end: it flows and settles like any other liquid the moment it exists. Nothing consumes it yet, the same shape residue and burntResidue shipped in before their own machines existed.
elements.name: moltenSand

reactions.note: Spec 5.3's worked example. Both cells become product, so a reaction changes composition without changing how many cells hold matter.
